slides.title: Cohort Studio
slides.notes: Pinned commit 54aeacb6f6f355a1dcaa42d7abf2ce174315ad69. Source review only; no live demonstration or official score.

slides.title: 1 · Unknown checksum verification is counted as a pass
slides.fix: Use a three-state check: verified True, mismatch False, and unavailable/unknown.
slides.notes: When sources.csv or an expected entry is missing, file_status retains verified=None. The verdict rejects only verified is False; otherwise it claims every used raw file matches the frozen checksums. Missing verification and successful verification are not equivalent. Committed manifests are separately marked unverified. Acceptance: Remove only the expected checksum entry from a synthetic fixture. The provenance check must become unknown without inventing a mismatch or pass.

slides.title: 2 · Request text is inserted into generated Python source
slides.fix: Serialize request text as a Python string literal with repr or a JSON value, rather than interpolating it into source delimiters.
slides.notes: The reproduction script inserts the raw request inside a triple-quoted module docstring. A request containing triple quotes can terminate that string, damage the script or introduce Python source. This is a source-identified code-generation hazard; no malicious generated file was executed. Acceptance: Use quotes, backslashes, newlines and a harmless marker as request text. Parse the output with ast.parse and verify the request remains data only.

slides.title: 3 · Automatic fixes are enabled by default in the API
slides.fix: Separate draft, preview and accepted execution states.
slides.notes: build_cohort defaults fix=True, applies inflation fixes and exports the resulting cohort. The first result and fix log are retained, which is useful. CLI/MCP consumers can nevertheless receive a changed analysis without an explicit per-change acceptance step. This is an authority and communication improvement, not a claim that all inflation fixes are wrong. Acceptance: An inflating join produces a proposed correction and two distinct versions; the user can inspect and accept or reject it before an approved export.

slides.title: 4 · Blocked outputs are exported beside ordinary cohorts
slides.fix: Bundle a manifest binding files to verdict, limitations, review state and hashes.
slides.notes: write_all writes cohort_samples.csv regardless of the verdict; the verdict is in a separate JSON. Exporting blocked cohorts can be useful for diagnosis, but the CSV alone loses the restriction. The report must not imply that a generated file is approved for use. Acceptance: Produce a blocked cohort, move its CSV alone and inspect the export contract. Ensure downstream tools can detect missing approval metadata.

slides.title: 5 · Automatic drafting can use a hosted service by default
slides.fix: Give a first-use routing notice or explicit opt-in.
slides.notes: ai=auto tries an own model, then the hosted service, then rules. The README explains this and --rules provides a local-only route; it is not hidden in documentation. A scientist may still reasonably assume a local CLI will not transmit their typed question. Acceptance: Mock both providers and verify ai=off makes no outbound request; an auto request displays provider selection before transmission.

slides.title: What is verified so far
slides.fix: Read the report; reproduce each issue with a positive control.
slides.notes: Parsing is not testing. No hosted app, clinical claims, real data or sealed inputs were verified. No numeric score.
